newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mostly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mostly higher in thin trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mostly higher Tuesday in tandem with stronger natural gas futures and spot cash market prices in the western U.S.
Most brokers and traders shrugged off the day's slight gain, and instead emphasized the light volume and overall lack of direction of the complex.
"Palo Verde is just making an (technical) adjustment," said one western futures trader. "We're in the middle of a February slump. No one wants to do anything."
March California-Oregon Border (COB) futures finished up 10 cents at $10.95 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing between $10.85 and $11.00.
April COB settled up 10 cents at $10.20. Most active COB contracts ended five to 15 cents higher.
March Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 12 cents at $13.22 after traded as high as $13.50. Most PV months were inactive today.

Peak, firm day-ahead power prices today at COB rose $1.25 to $12.50-13.50/MWh, and those at PV increased 25 cents to $1 to $13.50-14.00 on tighter supply availability due to several unplanned plant outages.
NYMEX March Henry Hub natural gas futures settled up 5.7 cents at $2.224 per million British thermal units.
In the western gas market, March deliveries at the Sumas export point on U.S./Canada border ended the day at $1.65-1.72 and at the San Juan Basin area in the Southwest $1.81-$1.84.
Barring any fresh news, the electricity complex will likely continue its thin, rangebound activity, most brokers and traders said.

For the Pacific Northwest, forecasts showed temperatures would average near normal into next week with below normal readings expected for the westernmost areas. Precipitation would likely be above-normal for most of the area with normal levels expected for the north-central part of the area.

For the Southwest, the latest six to 10 day outlook indicated the western and southern sections of the region would enjoy above-normal temperatures. Precipitation is expected to average below normal for much of the region.

Separately, restart of a 755 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was postponed to Wednesday from today for additionally repairs after tripping off line Sunday.
The 1,100 MW pumped storage hydroelectric Helms plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut Feb 1 for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for another week.
NYMEX estimated 231 COB and 88 PV contracts were sold, up from Monday's sales of 77 COB and 61 PV lots.
